institutionName: University of Natural Resources and Life Sciences, Vienna (BOKU)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Due to the covid situation I had to choose a country in Europe in last minute. I chose Austria over other European countries bacause of the nature and the specialization of the university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Overall it was a great experience, and I would recommend everyone to do it. I think it is very healthy to see something different and try to be in another system than you are use to in Denmark. 
It was a great university, with so many different courses.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was okay, I got a lot of information mails and a checklist before arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
We had an introduction day to see the university and meet some of the other exchange students.
The Erasmus coordinator and students from the host university as "tutors".

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing on WG gesucht.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you like to be social I would recommend living with others in a shared flat. Either with locals or other exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I lived with a local who could tell me about Vienna and what to see.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
It was pretty overwhelming in the beginning, with all the different courses and how to plan them. It is a very different system than KU, but not necessarily worse, it's just more loose.
It can be a little challenging finding courses to fill out a mandatory course, since the ECTS potins are so different.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You start finding the coursea you think are interesting before you leave and get them pre-approved. Not all of the courses are available at the time of departure on the BOKU online system, so it is just an idea of what you are interested in. The courses have few ECTS points compared to KU so it seems like a lot. It is probably not possible to se when the courses lie in the week, so you will have to wait till you get there.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Erasmus coordinator in the host university or you can write emails to the professors of the courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: There are so many great courses, so I endned up being satisfied with them. It can be a little challenging finding out which courses you are not allowed to take if you are on the bachelor.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: DON'T stress about the course registration and pre-approvals, you change it when you are there.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Since the courses are so much smaller you don't have a lot of time to immerse into the subjects.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very different among the courses. Some was more interactive, some were just lectures, LAB courses, student presentations

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Exploratory data analysis with R
First Steps with R 
Statistical growth models
Statistics with R
Foresights - what future to expect? (Late lessons from early warnings) 
Plant and environment 
Sustainable land use in developing countries  
Conservation biology 
Biodiversity crisis –climate crisis
Ecology of roots and mycorrhizae I
Ecology of roots and mycorrhizae II
Field camp I -introduction to mountain forestry and forest sciences

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Foresights - what future to expect? (Late lessons from early warnings): great course on future scenarios and perspectives of the world. Very inspiring and different.

Field camp I -introduction to mountain forestry and forest sciences: fantastic upportunity to meet other exchange students and to go on amazing trips. If you are not into forestry you should still do it for the social aspect. 

Exploratory data analysis with R: If you would like to work with R in a different and more creative way.

Cafés and bars are cheeper.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Before the covid lockdows it was great. Unfortunately I didn't get the full experience.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Museums are a must see in Vienna, they are great. I can also recommend getting last minute tickets cheap for the Opera to see it on the inside.
There is a lot of sports and teams to join on
USI.at
, but you have to be fast! Find out when the registration opens and be ready.
There is table tennis tables everywhere, so bring bats if you have.
The exchange environment is great and everyone is open minded. In the beginning of the stay BOKU arrange some great social events.
There is good bouldering upportunities for all levels.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: See above.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Hike!
The nature is beautiful and it is easy to get to amazing locations by train.
Skiing if you are there in the winter season.
Visiting neighbouring countries.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. People are nice.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: You could get a "buddy" or live with locals.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Supermarkets close early and are closed on sundays.
The physical paperwork and the use of cash.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
The beautiful buildings and grant museums. It is a beautiful city!
Good local wine.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't stress about the course registration.
Enjoy the natore around Vienna.
Appreciate meeting student from other countries.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
If you want to go on trips out of Vienna, buy the ÖBB vorteilskarte to get discounts on trains out of Vienna.
Take the train and bring your bike.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living in another country and experience the culture. Meeting other excange students.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Covid19.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
